Xi: Head-of-state diplomacy 'irreplaceable' for China-US ties
President urges maintaining momentum of stable growth in bilateral relationship
By CAO DESHENG in Shenzhen, Guangdong | China Daily
Updated: 2026-11-20 07:04
Share - WeChat
President Xi Jinping meets with United States President Donald Trump on Thursday in Shenzhen, Guangdong province. YAN YAN/XINHUA
President Xi Jinping highlighted on Thursday the "irreplaceable" role of head-of-state diplomacy in guiding relations between China and the United States, urging concrete actions to sustain the current momentum of stable and positive growth in the relationship.
Xi made the remarks during his meeting with US President Donald Trump in Shenzhen, Guangdong province, on the sidelines of the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation Economic Leaders' Meeting.
Both sides considered the meeting to be positive and constructive, according to a statement released after the meeting.
The two sides agreed to map out an action plan for building a constructive relationship of strategic stability, implement the consensus reached by the two presidents, and build a constructive China-US relationship of strategic stability on the basis of respect, fairness and reciprocity, the statement said.
This was the third meeting between Xi and Trump this year. The two presidents also met in Beijing in May, when Trump made a state visit to China, and in Washington in September, when Xi made a state visit to the US.
Xi said that over the past few months, he and Trump have been working together to explore the right path for China and the US, the two major countries, to get along well with each other.
The new vision of building a constructive China-US relationship of strategic stability based on respect, fairness and reciprocity has been well recognized by the peoples of both countries and welcomed by the international community, he said.
Xi noted that the overall stability and positive momentum of China-US relations have brought tangible benefits to the people of the two countries, and injected stability and certainty into the world.
He expressed his hope to continue working with Trump to jointly steer the giant ship of China-US relations in the right direction toward the future.
Xi emphasized that building a constructive China-US relationship of strategic stability is an unprecedented, groundbreaking endeavor that requires an enterprising spirit, hard and solid efforts, and the ability to get things done.
To sustain the current momentum of stable and positive growth in China-US relations, the key is to take concrete action to implement the consensus reached by the two heads of state, he said, adding that communication between the working teams on both sides also needs to keep pace.
Xi stressed that it is important to make a longer list of cooperation and a shorter list of problems. Differences that cannot be resolved for the time being should be managed in a constructive way to prevent them from escalating, he said.
On the Taiwan question, Xi said the US should keep doing the right thing and avoid major setbacks in China-US relations.
He called on the two sides to strengthen communication on economic and trade matters, address each other's concerns and work toward mutual benefit.
Cooperation between the two countries on counternarcotics, repatriation of illegal immigrants, and combating telecommunications and online fraud has yielded positive results, Xi said, adding that it can be further deepened based on respect, fairness and reciprocity.
He also underlined the need for China and the US to strengthen communication and coordination to guard against security risks of artificial intelligence and ensure that AI always remains under human control.
Trump said he and Xi have jointly guided the development of US-China relations, adding that both leaders have maintained close contact, with their friendship growing stronger.
Trade and investment ties between the two countries have continued to grow, and cooperation on fentanyl and other issues has yielded results, Trump noted.
Both sides should maintain the momentum of steady development of bilateral relations, and strengthen cooperation in areas such as farm products, energy and super intelligence, and fairly address each other's concerns, Trump said.
He told Xi that the US does not support "Taiwan independence".
Trump congratulated China on hosting a successful APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting, adding that both countries need to work together to lead and promote world peace and stability.
The two presidents also discussed regional and international issues of mutual interest.
He Yadong, spokesman for the Chinese Ministry of Commerce, announced on Thursday that the agricultural working group under the China-US Board of Trade will soon hold its first meeting.
The two countries' economic and trade teams have maintained communication at various levels, and the two sides held the first meeting of the Board of Trade under the China-US economic and trade consultation mechanism via video link on Nov 13, the spokesman said at a regular news briefing in Beijing.

Updated: 2026-11-21 08:29
Share - WeChat
President Xi Jinping meets with Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim on Friday in Shenzhen, Guangdong province. SHEN HONG/XINHUA

Xi recalled that he and Anwar reached important consensus on building a high-level strategic China-Malaysia community with a shared future in April last year.
China is ready to work with Malaysia to uphold the original aspiration of establishing diplomatic ties, foster greater momentum for cooperation and further advance the building of a China-Malaysia community with a shared future to bring greater benefits to both peoples, Xi said.

China and Malaysia should maintain high-level strategic communication and support each other in safeguarding their respective national sovereignty, security and development interests, Xi said. Xi called for joint efforts to advance the reform of global governance, strengthen coordination and cooperation within multilateral frameworks, and safeguard common interests.
Anwar said the Taiwan question is China's internal affair, and Malaysia firmly adheres to the one-China policy.
He said Malaysia is ready to strengthen strategic coordination with China, give full play to the role of bilateral cooperation mechanisms, ensure the sound operation of key infrastructure projects and enhance cooperation in emerging areas such as artificial intelligence.

NEWS China’s Cargo Drones Take Off With Two Successful Trials
Two domestic companies successfully carried out flight and delivery tests of unmanned aircraft designed for cargo and emergency deliveries in the last week.
By He Qitong
Nov 20, 2026 # technology
China has successfully tested two large unmanned cargo aircraft: one with a 5-ton payload capacity and the other capable of flying 3,000 kilometers, laying the groundwork for future commercial and emergency transportation systems.
On Tuesday, the country announced that the Changying-8, a domestically developed unmanned cargo aircraft, had completed a test delivery. Three days prior, another domestically developed unmanned cargo aircraft, the W5000, also completed its maiden flight.
The milestones come as China’s drone market is expected to exceed 140 billion yuan ($19.6 billion) by the end of 2026, with the industrial drone segment alone projected to reach 84 billion yuan, up 12.5% from last year. 
China began testing large cargo drones as early as 2017 and incorporated the concept of the “ low-altitude economy ” into government policy in 2021. The Civil Aviation Administration of China has also laid out a roadmap to establish an air transportation system for unmanned aircraft by 2035.
During its delivery test, the Changying-8, developed by China North Industries Group Corporation, released a cargo pallet at an altitude of 300 meters before returning to its base.
The aircraft, whose maiden flight took place in Zhengzhou, capital of the central Henan province, on March 31, has a maximum range of over 3,000 kilometers, measures 17 meters in length, has a 25-meter wingspan, and an 18-cubic-meter cargo compartment volume, domestic media reported. 
In the event of extreme disasters such as earthquakes, floods, and mudslides destroying roads and bridges, the aircraft can be used to transport up to 3.5 metric tons of goods, equal to over 700 disaster-relief tents, the head of the Changying-8’s development team told state news agency Xinhua.
According to its engineers, future applications could include transportation of regional cargo, emergency supplies, and cold-chain deliveries, domestic media reported.
On Saturday, the W5000, an unmanned cargo aircraft developed by Chinese aviation company Air White Whale, also completed its maiden flight in northern China’s Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region.
The aircraft flew for about 30 minutes at an altitude of 1,000 meters, completing a series of test maneuvers before landing. The test focused on the aircraft’s flight stability and the coordinated operation of its propulsion, flight control, electronics, and ground-based monitoring and control systems.
With a maximum payload capacity of 5 metric tons, the W5000 is billed as one of the world’s largest unmanned cargo aircraft by payload capacity. Made of carbon fiber and weighing less than 6 metric tons, the aircraft measures over 22 meters in both length and wingspan and can fly at a cruising speed of 526 kilometers per hour, with a maximum range of 2,600 kilometers, domestic media reported. 
Hu Zhendong, founder, chairman, and CEO of Air White Whale, said the W5000 could reduce logistics costs per ton-kilometer by more than 60% compared with comparable crewed cargo aircraft.
The W5000 is expected to begin commercial operation by the end of next year, according to domestic media.
Editor: Marianne Gunnarsson.

NEWS China’s Basic Insurance to Cover CAR T-Cell Cancer Therapy
The treatment, which involves modifying a patient’s own cells to fight blood cancer, will be eligible for partial reimbursement beginning Jan. 1.
By Chen Yiru
Nov 17, 2026 # health
China will include a CAR T-cell therapy in its national health insurance scheme for the first time, making a blood cancer treatment that once cost over 1 million yuan ($150,000) per dose more accessible. 
The National Healthcare Security Administration announced on Nov. 14 that relmacabtagene autoleucel, or relma-cel, made by Shanghai-based biotech firm JW Therapeutics and sold under the brand name Carteyva, will be covered by insurance starting Jan. 1. The therapy has three approved uses for different types of lymphoma and costs 1.29 million yuan per dose.
CAR T-cell therapy is primarily used to treat types of lymphoma and involves extracting and genetically modifying a patient’s own immune cells to target cancer cells, before infusing them back into the body. China approved its first CAR T-cell therapy product in 2021.
Most of China’s population is covered by the country’s national insurance scheme: 1.33 billion were enrolled in basic medical insurance by the end of 2025. Only drugs listed in the national insurance catalog can be partially reimbursed through the medical insurance fund. For drugs not listed, patients must usually bear 100% of the cost. 
For years, CAR T-cell drugs were excluded from the national insurance list because an unwritten industry rule held that drugs priced above 300,000 yuan rarely secured coverage, limiting patient access, according to Shanghai-based media outlet The Paper.
The rate of CAR T-cell drug use as a second-line treatment for large B-cell lymphoma in China is about one-sixth of that in the United States, while use as a third-line treatment is about one-10th of the rate in the U.S. and Europe.
Carteyva was one of five CAR T-cell therapies included last year in China’s first commercial insurance list for high-cost innovative drugs. This year, those drugs became eligible for national coverage. Two CAR T-cell drug manufacturers, including JW Therapeutics, entered insurance coverage negotiations on Sept. 6.
“Two or three years ago, we wouldn’t have dared to imagine this,” Tian Feng, JW Therapeutics chairman and CEO, told The Paper.
China records about 101,500 new lymphoma cases each year. Carteyva is available at more than 200 certified hospitals nationwide.
The updated national reimbursement list adds 107 drugs covering oncology, chronic diseases, mental illnesses, rare diseases, and pediatric medications. A separate commercial insurance list, which covers drugs outside the basic scheme, includes 12 new treatments.
“This is a historic moment for lymphoma patients in China,” Tian said, adding that when he and the company received the news, “everyone really felt that the treatment of lymphoma patients in China had entered a new, very exciting era.”

The rate of CAR T-cell drug use as a second-line treatment for large B-cell lymphoma in China is about one-sixth of that in the United States, while use as a third-line treatment is about one-10th of the rate in the U.S. and Europe.

Carteyva was one of five CAR T-cell therapies included last year in China’s first commercial insurance list for high-cost innovative drugs. This year, those drugs became eligible for national coverage. Two CAR T-cell drug manufacturers, including JW Therapeutics, entered insurance coverage negotiations on Sept. 6.
“Two or three years ago, we wouldn’t have dared to imagine this,” Tian Feng, JW Therapeutics chairman and CEO, told The Paper.
China records about 101,500 new lymphoma cases each year. Carteyva is available at more than 200 certified hospitals nationwide.

The updated national reimbursement list adds 107 drugs covering oncology, chronic diseases, mental illnesses, rare diseases, and pediatric medications. A separate commercial insurance list, which covers drugs outside the basic scheme, includes 12 new treatments.

“This is a historic moment for lymphoma patients in China,” Tian said, adding that when he and the company received the news, “everyone really felt that the treatment of lymphoma patients in China had entered a new, very exciting era.”

By Cai Yiwen
Jul 16, 2026 # history # TV & film # business # literature
This year, Chaoshan found itself in the national spotlight. Located in eastern Guangdong province on China’s southern coast, the region unexpectedly became one of the country’s biggest cultural talking points. During Chinese New Year, travelers flocked there in search of “authentic” New Year traditions. Soon after, a low-budget film set in Chaoshan became a surprise national hit. Spoken largely in the Teochew dialect, which is unintelligible to most Chinese audiences, and centered on a little-known episode of local history, the film sparked widespread curiosity about the region and its culture.
Yet this renewed fascination only scratches the surface.
Chaoshan’s influence extends far beyond what its geographic size might suggest. For centuries, Chaoshan has looked outward. Waves of migration carried its merchants across Southeast Asia and beyond, creating one of the world’s most influential Chinese business and diaspora networks. At the same time, it has remained one of China’s strongest bastions of traditional culture, where ancestral rituals, lineage ties, and local customs continue to shape everyday life.

That combination has made Chaoshan one of China’s most distinctive regional cultures and given it an outsized role in China’s modern history. Its overseas networks helped connect China to global markets, capital, and ideas, while its enduring kinship ties and cultural traditions reveal how local identities have persisted through decades of rapid economic and social change.

by jasondavies
Related: Levent Alpöge claims proof of the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis [pdf] - https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50574968
Aurornis: The manuscript claims he has been working on this problem for 12 years. I can only imagine the feelings that must have hit him when he saw the Anthropic announcement. Though if he believed he had solved it, he must have known it was only a matter of time until one of the AI companies found it, too. A hurried announcement with the draft published within hours is the only way to claim a tie to the discovery. Time will tell if either holds up under further analysis, but at least he has shown his hand to the world with a timestamp on it now.
prometheus1992: Is it possible that brian conrad somehow uploaded the proof to anthropic to cross check something and then the anthropic guys got the proof? - it doesn't have to be the full proof - even if portions were uploaded, that should also be enough or at least calls for a thorough check on ants side. the human proof has been in the works for 12 years, who knows when something was uploaded somewhere or some info just stayed on a google drive which was later sold.
jc_811: Hey can someone familiar here explain the why the GRH is such a big deal to mathematics? What will this allow us to unlock? Will it have any effect on the general population?
kyykky: While ago, there used to be a world where a person, with large enough brain capacity, could earn a living simply by being smart. That is no more the case. Earning your living by intellectual endeavour will require an access to a machine which is not controlled by you, not controlled by the government representing you, but rather a group of very rich individuals who may just decide to bar your access. Perhaps you attempted something they do not approve, perhaps it was just a mistake. In any case, it is hard to claim that you still have control.
Kotlopou: This looks crazy? 940 pages and the very first section 1.1.1 is empty. I can see why the author wanted to polish it. Let's just hope somebody clears this up somehow. But at the same time Brian Conrad is presumably not a crank (per Wikipedia he worked with Wiles on FLT), but at the same time it seems insane to try and keep a 940-page result for a year hidden from public view in the current mathematical climate. Somewhere around this summer, the world stopped being comprehensible...
rlt: Mathematicians should start regularly posting hashes of their in-progress work with verifiable timestamps to at least claim partial credit when AI solves the problem they've been working on.
pbkompasz: 900 pages vs 250,000 pages Compression is intelligence
dimator: What a gut wrenching experience this must be, to work on something for 12 years and have it snatched out of your fingertips. And on top of that that something is one of the most important open questions in mathematics. Absolutely heartbreaking for that guy.

I Don't Trust Visual Recordings Anymore. But One Day I Will Again
https://spectrum.ieee.org/fighting-back-against-deep-fakes
by jnord
fedpost: These signing schemes are a very long way off right now. Even if they get widely adopted and if they aren't subverted immediately, it's going to take a decade or more for widespread adoption. Most of the "crazy shit" footage you see online is from an old cellphone that's not getting replaced any time soon.
lowbloodsugar: Do we imagine that the keys from a DSLR or phone can’t be extracted by a sufficiently motivated actor? Or that the sensor on such a device couldn’t be replaced with a substitute image generator?
nayuki: > Credentials that follow the C2PA standard, for example, attach a cryptographically signed manifest to a photo or video at the moment of capture; this metadata records the device, the time and location of the recording This claim sounds like a tidy solution, but my gut feeling is that it doesn't really solve the problem. I struggle to articulate exactly why I think it's wrong, but I'll list some ideas: * The camera presumably holds an asymmetric private key. The camera is in the user's hands, and chips could be removed and examined to extract the key with immense difficulty. Extremely few people in this world have the knowledge and equipment to do this, but it only takes one person to break the system for everyone. * The camera maker might leak the key through negligence. Look at other examples where companies leaked TLS/SSL private keys or other cryptographic secrets. * This scheme seems to give a lot of power to a small number of companies to define image authenticity in a proprietary way. This gatekeeping doesn't seem like a good direction for society. * If someone is determined to break the system, eventually someone does. Look at the history of DRM and how countless schemes have been broken. Look at how Intel SGX was broken (it claims to allow a CPU to execute secret computations on behalf of someone else without the physical hardware owner being able to inspect those computations). * Some image authentication schemes were cracked, such as ElcomSoft breaking an older version of Canon's scheme in the year 2010. * What if a genuine camera takes a real photo of a real film slide or electronic monitor displaying utterly ridiculous imagery? (Analogous to the analog hole for DRM.) * Does the private key have an expiration date? At any given point in time, is there an assumption that all photos older than a certain time have unreliable signatures? (Think of how the TLS certificate authority infrastructure comes with expiration dates.) I don't have the answers to this problem. One thing I want to suggest, though, is that images coming straight off a camera have a lot of detail, and I think that is hard for AI to fake. Faking an image at Instagram resolution with relatively high JPEG compression seems plausible. Faking 6000×4000 pixels (24 MP) without leaving telltale seams and artifacts is a lot harder. I say this as someone who does digital photography and spends a lot of time pixel-peeping. > The types of forensic analyses that I routinely perform do not currently operate at internet scale and speed. Fair point. But I don't think you can tech-shortcut your way out of this problem. > These provenance signals are often criticized as being only a partial solution or vulnerable to attack. This is true if we think of them as mechanisms for catching bad actors. But that’s not what they’re supposed to do. Their purpose is to let good actors prove that their audiovisual recording is what it claims to be. You're being too charitable. It only takes one bad actor, one successful cracker to destroy the foundations of authenticity. One credibly signed fake image is enough to cast doubt on all the signed real images out there.
aidenn0: I'm sure it will be no harder to get loose keys for C2PA as it is to get keys for bluray playback.
garaetjjte: Yeah, just go all in on implementing another nightmare dystopian technology. Not only you will get unfairly disadvantaged when filming on older hardware, consider also misinformation capabilities granted to big corps and state actors: look, this video evidence is totally authentic, it has all the right signatures! ...nevermind that we got the signing keys through NSL from camera manufacturer.
minebreaker: > To believe a recording is real now, it must also carry a provenance signal from the point of recording. I really don't understand these approaches. As if what the poor little girl Nayirah saw was deepfaked? How can a chip in a camera make it more true ?
isomorphic: > [...] the deepfake-video-call software has to take shortcuts, such as simplifying faces and how they interact with their surroundings, and allowing some drift between audio and video or between video frames. The human eye doesn’t notice the shortcuts, but we can forensically expose them. ...for now.

Environment: Windows server 2003, Spring 3.0, Tomcat 6 How can I reference a JNDI property inside a PropertyPlaceholderConfigurer? My problem seems to be how to reference JNDI resources inside the tag pair Thanks in advance! Mark
Your approach may not work Mark, this is because PropertyPlaceHolderConfigurer is a BeanFactoryPostProcessor and gets invoked at the point when the bean definitions are created, whereas the jndi lookup happens post this stage. I saw an older Spring forum discussion item, which has a recommendation for an approach of using a jndi lookup based properties file, which may suit your needs:
I believe you will have to do something like this . I haven't tested it but basically the setLocations method in PropertyPlaceholderConfigurer takes in an array of Resource(In our case UrlResource - http://static.springsource.org/spring/docs/2.0.x/api/org/springframework/core/io/UrlResource.html ) which in turn has a constructor with the file path . <jee:jndi-lookup id="mypropsfile1" jndi-name="myPropsFile1" default-value="file:///C:/defaultPath" resource-ref="true"/> <jee:jndi-lookup id="mypropsfile2" jndi-name="myPropsFile2" resource-ref="true"/> <bean id="propertyConfigurer" class="org.springframework.beans.factory.config.PropertyPlaceholderConfigurer" depends-on="mypropsfile1,mypropsfile2"> <property name="ignoreUnresolvablePlaceholders" value="true"/> <property name="locations"> <list> <bean class="org.springframework.core.io.UrlResource"> <constructor-arg><ref bean="mypropsfile1"/></constructor-arg> </bean> <bean class="org.springframework.core.io.UrlResource"> <constructor-arg><ref bean="myPropsFile2"/></constructor-arg> </bean> </list> </property> </bean> I am not sure if there is a tag called in spring . Check this http://static.springsource.org/spring/docs/3.0.x/spring-framework-reference/html/beans.html#beans-introduction
I do this in Spring 3 using a map as follows: <jee:jndi-lookup id="myJndiLookup" jndi-name="com.techtrip.spring.config.myJndiLookup"></jee:jndi-lookup> <bean id="somethingWithMap" class="com.techtrip.foo.SomethingWithMap"> <property name="propMap"> <map> <entry key="myJndiLookup" value-ref="myJndiLookup" /> </map> </property> </bean> This works fine in most cases. You may run into trouble if you use AOP or something that wraps the bean in a Proxy class even if you set eager init correctly. Algorithm for path simplification and smoothing of 2D trajectories
I'm searching for an algorithm for path simplification and smoothing for 2D trajectories. So I have a ordered list of 2D points. These points should be simplified, e.g. with the Ramer–Douglas–Peucker algorithm. But the output must be smooth, so the resulting path should be constructed from Bezier curves or splines. Is there any modification of the Ramer–Douglas–Peucker algorithm which could handle this? I found a path simplification algorithm in the paper.js library, which does exactly what I'm searching for: http://paperjs.org/examples/path-simplification/ But I was not able to understand the algorithm from the undocumented javascript source code.
The work you want to do falls into the category of "curve fitting". There are tons of different algorithms for curve fitting but almost all curve fitting algorithms can be divided into two different categories: interpolation and approximation. Interpolation algorithms produce a curve that passes through all the data points exactly while approximation algorithms generate a curve that lies close to the data points. Of course, hybrid algorithms also exist. Since you want the data points to be smoothed, you should be looking for approximation algorithms. For the two algorithms you mentioned: RDP algorithm and Schneider algorithm (the one in Paper.js), they are both approximation algorithms. So, basically you can use either of them. For RDP, after obtaining the simplified path, you can use create a Catmull Rom spline or Overhauser spline thru the vertices of the simplified path to obtain a smooth curve. However, you don't have direct control for the deviation between the resulting spline and the vertices in the original path. For Schneider algorithm, it will starts with fitting the data points by a cubic Bezier curve with end tangent constraints. If the deviation to the resulting curve is too large, then it will split the data points into two "regions" and fit each region of data with a cubic Bezier curves with end tangent constraints. This process will be repeated until the deviation to all cubic Bezier curves are small enough. As a result, it produces a series of cubic Bezier curves connected at best with C1 continuity (very likely it is actually G1 only). Furthermore, since this algorithm evaluate the end tangents from original data points, the noise in the data point will affect the end tangent evaluation and therefore the cubic Bezier fitting. If you can spent time in the topic of curve fitting, you should look into least square fitting with B-spline curves. This will generate an output curve with high continuity (C2 for cubic B-spline curves for example). If you don't have much time to spent, then Schneider's algorithm is a good choice that strikes a balance between the implementation cost (if you have to re-implement it in a specific language) and the resulting curve's quality.
What you're trying to do is called curve fitting. fitting to a good-enough tolerance it's approximation/regression slower and approximate, though it usually reduces the point count, i.e: simplifies the path fitting through exact points it's called interpolation. faster and precise but offers no simplification The Ramer-Douglas-Peucker algorithm essentially smoothes visual 'noise' out of a polyline by removing unnecessary points within a specified tolerance, so while it does smooth out visual roughness, it's not actual smoothing to curve - a curve fitting algorithm will need to fit bezier curves either near or through those points. The paper.js part you mentioned is approximation. The underlying algorithm is Phillip Schneider's: "Algorithm for Automatically Fitting Digitized Curves" from Graphics Gems. For interpolation, there's many options floating around. A popular one is Catmull-Rom , especially the centripetal variant - this is mine in ES6 - but it's also merged into paper.js as the path.smooth({ method: 'catmull-rom', type: 0.5 }) Also, here is a very short discussion on the mailing list about path.simplify() decisions and here is an extensive discussion about path.smooth() decisions.

Balanced Ternary Division Algorithm
I have been writing a ternary computer emulator, and I have become stuck with the problem of implementing ternary integer division. On the most part, the basic mathematical operations follow the same logic as regular binary or decimal, and indeed division follows that mostly, except that you can't quite do it the same way, due to the possibility of three states and negative numbers, you need to adjust the result based on that. The Wikipedia article for ternary arithmetic is vague at best when talking about this, and there aren't many examples or other articles around. I found one other article (apologies but I managed to lose the link) that described a method with pseudocode, but I couldn't get it working. The Wikipedia page in question says: If the dividend is between the plus and minus of half the divisor, the trit of the quotient is 0 This is just word salad without any articles or pseudocode or anything to explain it, so was looking for a better source. I was wondering if someone could help me find some resources or papers to look at to help implementing this.
I'm afraid the C language does not support CPUs that would use ternary (or trinary) representation for integers or floating point values, balanced ternary using trits with (-1, 0, 1) values or unbalanced ternary (0, 1, 2). Binary representation is explicit in numerous parts of the C Standard, eg: 6.2.6.2 Integer types 1 For unsigned integer types the bits of the object representation shall be divided into two groups: value bits and padding bits. If there are N value bits, each bit shall represent a different power of 2 between 1 and 2 N−1 , so that objects of that type shall be capable of representing values from 0 to 2 N − 1 using a pure binary representation; this shall be known as the value representation. The values of any padding bits are unspecified. The number of value bits N is called the width of the unsigned integer type. Regarding your question, there is no such thing as ternary division : in C, division is defined in terms of basic arithmetics, it does not rely on the actual representation of values, only on the mathematical value and the range of the type. The shifting operators << and >> are defined in terms of the multiplication and division or modulo a power of 2. The only reference to binary is the number of bit in the representation, as in the above example. Other bitwise operators such as & , | and ^ would require a very contorted emulation on CPUs using trits to evaluate to the correct values. The Wikipedia article on Ternary computer has a lot of details on possible implementation details, some indeed obscure, and links to an actual computer designed in 1958 in Moscow: the Setun . A more recent attempt, the 5500FP seems available today, and I am tempted to order one to find out if it really exists and how it can be programmed :)

The shifting operators << and >> are defined in terms of the multiplication and division or modulo a power of 2. The only reference to binary is the number of bit in the representation, as in the above example. Other bitwise operators such as & , | and ^ would require a very contorted emulation on CPUs using trits to evaluate to the correct values. The Wikipedia article on Ternary computer has a lot of details on possible implementation details, some indeed obscure, and links to an actual computer designed in 1958 in Moscow: the Setun . A more recent attempt, the 5500FP seems available today, and I am tempted to order one to find out if it really exists and how it can be programmed :)

How to prevent VBA from creating a worksheet based on a list of values, if a sheet by that name already exists
I am adding new worksheets to a workbook whose name will be the value of rows in a column. In the column, there are or can be duplicate values. I want to skip the creation of a new worksheet for any duplicate values in that column in my VBA loop. How can I do this?
You can use a COUNT.IF function applied to the list down to the point you are currently focusing, using the content of your focused cell as criteria. Let's say you are currently focusing cell A4. The formula could be something like: =COUNTIF($A$2:A4,A4) Integrated in a code in VBA, it could become something like this: Option Explicit Sub SubTest() Dim DblRow As Double Dim RngList As Range Set RngList = Range("A2:A10") For DblRow = 1 To RngList.Rows.Count If Excel.WorksheetFunction.CountIf(Range(RngList(1, 1), RngList(DblRow, 1)), RngList(DblRow, 1).Value2) = 1 Then 'Do stuff Else 'Do nothing/something else End If Next End Sub
You could get a unique list of the values in an array, then loop through that to add the new sheets. Sub AddSheets() Dim wsNew As Worksheet Dim rng As Range Dim idx As Long Dim varNames As Variant ' assumes column A on Sheet1 has the values with the new worksheet names With Sheets("Sheet1") Set rng = .Range("A2", .Range("A" & Rows.Count).End(xlUp)) End With ' get unique values from column A in a 1D array varNames = Application.Transpose(Application.Unique(rng)) ' loop through array, add new sheets and name them For idx = LBound(varNames) To UBound(varNames) With ThisWorkbook Set wsNew = .Sheets.Add(after:=.Sheets(.Sheets.Count)) wsNew.Name = varNames(idx) End With Next idx End Sub
In your loop, check if worksheet name already exist against value.

How do I retrieve data from a database with PL/pgSQL?
I have a PL/pgSQL code block to retrieve data from a selected row in a dropdown list in the user interface. Even though I'm selecting values and assigning the result in a loop, the block doesn't emit them outside, ending up not returning anything it collected: do $$ DECLARE w_idCandidato int; w_numeroDaProva int; BEGIN FOR v_idCandidato, v_numeroDaProva IN SELECT pg."idCandidato", pg."numeroDaProva" FROM public."tb_provasGeradasProCandidato" AS pg INNER JOIN public."tb_candidatos" cd ON "idCandidato" = cd.id INNER JOIN public."tb_processosSeletivos" pr ON "idProcesso" = pr.id WHERE cd.id = 27 LOOP w_idCandidato := "idCandidato"; w_numeroDaProva := "numeroDaProva"; END LOOP; END; $$ How do I retrieve that data from this PL/pgSQL block?
"Doesn't works" is an inadequate problem description on all accounts. A DO statement can never RETURN data; for that, you would need a (set returning) function. But I don't see the point in using PL/pgSQL at all, if all you need is the result of a query.
DO doesn't return anything usable in your application. But you don't need a DO statement at all, no PL/pgSQL at all. You only need the SELECT statement, execute it, and fetch the result in your application. You're making simple things very complicated.
